chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, and Jameel ibn Darraj, and Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman who has a servant (slave) who has been immoral, so we need her milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Order her to give permission (for sexual relations), the milk will be good (permissible/clean).'

key_terms.فَلْتُحَلِّلْهَا: Let her give permission (for sexual relations)
key_terms.قَدْ فَجَرَتْ: She has been immoral/had illicit sex

ai.seo_question: How does sexual relations affect the permissibility of a slave woman's milk in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a specific fiqh ruling regarding the permissibility of consuming the milk of a female slave who has committed *zina* (unlawful sexual intercourse). The Imam instructs that she must be 'released' (i.e., granted permission for further sexual relations with her master) to purify her milk, rendering it *halal* and good for consumption. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of how sexual impurity affects the physical state of the body and its products, linking ritual purity to biological consumption.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin salim, and Jameel Bin Darraj, and sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the woman who happened to have a servant (slave) of hers who had been immoral, so we were needy for her milk. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Order her, so let her give permission, her milk is good’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a boy who impregnated my slave-girl who then gave birth and we needed her milk. If I give permission, will her milk be fine? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it will be fine.’”
